key_insight: O-kRystal learns orbital-informed corrections from cheap PBE calculations to predict higher-level band structures, achieving HSE06-level accuracy across diverse materials and even unseen k-points.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more scalable electronic-structure screening for semiconductors, correlated materials, and 2D systems without running full high-cost calculations everywhere.
method: Uses PBE as both an energy baseline and a source of real- and reciprocal-space orbital matrices.
Predicts state-by-state corrections to band energies as functions of crystal momentum and spin.
Trained at high-symmetry points, then generalized to band paths and dense Brillouin-zone density-of-states reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Across nearly 6,000 3D materials, the model predicts HSE06 band energies within 5 eV of the band-edge midpoint with 0.171 ± 0.009 eV MAE, and it also improves six strongly correlated materials by 68.7% over PBE.
watch_item: Accuracy may drop for states far from the band-edge window or for systems whose orbital character differs substantially from the training distribution.
paper_title: Beyond DFT electronic band structures via dual-space orbital learning
